name: San Jose
operatingHours: VTA light rail runs ~5:00 AM–~1:00 AM on weekdays and slightly shorter hours on weekends. Trains come every 15 min by day on weekdays and every 20 min on weekends, then every 30–60 min after ~8 PM. There is no all-night light rail.
fareInfo: An adult light rail or local bus ride is $2.50. Paying with Clipper or a contactless bank card includes 2 hours of transfers and caps at the $7.50 day-pass price. Station machines also sell a $5 8-hour light rail pass. The Route 60 Airport Flyer is free when boarding at SJC.

hotels.name: Residence Inn by Marriott San Jose Airport

sights.name: Winchester Mystery House
sights.note: Sarah Winchester's sprawling Victorian mansion, built nonstop for decades, full of staircases to nowhere and doors that open onto walls; seen on a guided tour.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM daily (some days to 4:00 PM); timed guided tours

sights.name: Municipal Rose Garden
sights.note: A free five-acre garden in the Rose Garden neighbourhood with thousands of roses around a central fountain, at its best from April to June.
sights.hours: 8:00 AM–1 hour after sunset daily; free

sights.name: Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum
sights.note: The largest collection of Egyptian artefacts on display in western North America, with mummies and a walk-through replica tomb, set in a temple-style park.
sights.hours: Fri 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sat–Sun 11:00 AM–6:00 PM; closed Mon–Thu

sights.name: The Tech Interactive
sights.note: A hands-on science and technology centre on Plaza de César Chávez where you can design, test and tinker, plus an IMAX dome theatre.
sights.hours: School year: Wed–Fri 10:00 AM–3:00 PM, Sat 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sun 11:00 AM–5:00 PM; closed Mon–Tue

sights.name: Cathedral Basilica of St. Joseph
sights.note: A domed 1870s cathedral on Market Street with stained glass and painted murals, an unexpectedly ornate interior in the downtown core.
sights.hours: Open daily ~7:00 AM–5:00 PM, around Mass times

sights.name: SAP Center
sights.note: Home arena of the NHL's San Jose Sharks and the city's main venue for big concerts, a short walk from Diridon station.

sights.name: Children's Discovery Museum of San Jose
sights.note: A bright purple building packed with play-based exhibits for young kids, from a water lab to a pretend fire truck.
sights.hours: School year: Tue–Fri 9:30 AM–1:00 PM, Sat–Sun 9:30 AM–4:30 PM; closed Mon

sights.name: Happy Hollow Park & Zoo
sights.note: A small zoo and amusement park aimed at children under ten, with gentle rides, a puppet theatre and red pandas and lemurs.
sights.hours: Thu–Sat 10:00 AM–4:00 PM (reduced schedule; check before visiting)

sights.name: Japanese Friendship Garden
sights.note: A koi-pond garden in Kelley Park modelled on Okayama's Korakuen, San Jose's sister city, with bridges, a waterfall and lanterns.

sights.name: History Park
sights.note: An open-air collection of restored and replica buildings from old San Jose, including a trolley barn, print shop and a half-scale electric light tower.
sights.hours: Grounds open daily; historic buildings open ~Sat–Sun 11:00 AM–4:00 PM

sights.name: San Pedro Square Market
sights.note: An indoor-outdoor food hall in a historic block downtown, with dozens of vendors, bars and a lively courtyard in the evenings.

sights.name: San José Museum of Art
sights.note: A modern and contemporary art museum in a former 1890s post office next to the cathedral, with rotating exhibitions focused on West Coast artists.
sights.hours: Tue–Thu and Sat–Sun 11:00 AM–6:00 PM, Fri 11:00 AM–9:00 PM; closed Mon

sights.name: Plaza de César Chávez
sights.note: The palm-lined central square of downtown, with a fountain children play in and the city's winter holiday market and rink.

sights.name: Japantown
sights.note: One of only three historic Japantowns left in the US, a few walkable blocks of family-run shops, sushi bars, temples and a Sunday farmers' market.
sights.hours: Open street; most shops ~11:00 AM–6:00 PM; farmers' market Sun ~8:30 AM–noon

sights.name: Willow Glen
sights.note: A leafy residential neighbourhood whose Lincoln Avenue main street is lined with independent boutiques, cafés and restaurants.
sights.hours: Open street; shops ~10:00 AM–8:00 PM, restaurants later

sights.name: Alum Rock Park
sights.note: California's oldest municipal park, a wooded canyon in the eastern foothills with creekside trails and old mineral springs.

railStations.name: San Jose Diridon
railStations.note: San Jose's 1935 main station: Caltrain to San Francisco (~1–1.5 h), Amtrak Capitol Corridor and Coast Starlight, and ACE. The VTA Green Line stops here and downtown is ~1.2 km east; SAP Center is next door.
railStations.hours: Station open ~4:30 AM–~1:00 AM; trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: San José Mineta International Airport
airports.transitNote: Not on the light rail map. The free VTA Route 60 Airport Flyer runs from Terminals A and B to Metro/Airport station (Blue and Green lines, ~10 min) every ~15–30 min, and light rail then takes ~15 min to downtown. Route 60 also continues to Santa Clara Caltrain station.
airports.hours: Route 60 ~5:00 AM–~midnight; light rail at Metro/Airport ~5:00 AM–~1:00 AM.
